questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A newly graduated nurse understands that professional nursing practice is based primarily on:

options.text: Delivering safe, ethical and evidence-informed patient care
Working independently without consulting colleagues
Completing documentation at the end of the shift
Following doctors' instructions only

questions.rationale: Professional nursing practice requires nurses to provide safe, ethical, patient-centred and evidence-informed care while working collaboratively with the healthcare team. Nurses are accountable for their own professional decisions and actions.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse is preparing to administer medication but notices that the patient's identification band is missing. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Administer the medication because the patient is familiar.
Stop the medication administration until the patient's identity is confirmed.
Ask the patient's family to confirm the identity.
Ask another nurse if they know the patient.

questions.rationale: Correct patient identification is one of the most important patient safety principles. Medication should never be administered until the patient's identity has been verified using approved identification procedures.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which behaviour best demonstrates professional accountability?

options.text: Reporting a medication error immediately.
Ignoring a near miss because no harm occurred.
Asking another nurse to document observations.
Waiting until the end of the shift to report an incident.

questions.rationale: Accountability means accepting responsibility for one's professional actions, including reporting errors or near misses promptly to protect patient safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Patient confidentiality means:

options.text: Discussing patient information in public areas.
Allowing family members unrestricted access to all medical information.
Discussing patient information only with friends.
Sharing information only with authorised healthcare professionals involved in the patient's care.

questions.rationale: Patient information must only be shared with authorised healthcare professionals directly involved in providing care, while maintaining privacy and confidentiality.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse notices another staff member using inappropriate language towards a patient. What is the nurse's professional responsibility?

options.text: Report the behaviour according to organisational policy.
Wait until another nurse notices.
Discuss the incident with other patients.
Ignore the situation.

questions.rationale: Professional nurses advocate for respectful and safe patient care. Unprofessional behaviour should be addressed and reported through the appropriate organisational channels.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best reflects patient-centred care?

options.text: The patient is actively involved in decisions about their care.
The healthcare team decides what is best without consulting the patient.
The nurse makes all healthcare decisions.
Family members always make healthcare decisions.

questions.rationale: Patient-centred care recognises the patient's right to participate in decisions affecting their health and wellbeing.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse realises they are unfamiliar with a newly introduced medical device. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Refuse to care for the patient.
Ask another nurse to operate it without supervision.
Use the equipment and learn while caring for the patient.
Seek appropriate training or guidance before using the equipment.

questions.rationale: Professional nurses recognise the limits of their competence and seek assistance or training before performing unfamiliar procedures.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which action best demonstrates respect for cultural diversity?

options.text: Assuming patients from the same country have identical beliefs.
Ignoring cultural practices that differ from the nurse's own beliefs.
Asking patients about their cultural preferences and incorporating them into care whenever possible.
Providing identical care to every patient regardless of individual beliefs.

questions.rationale: Culturally competent nursing involves respecting each patient's individual beliefs, values, and preferences while planning care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Professional communication within the healthcare team is important because it:

options.text: Reduces documentation requirements.
Replaces written documentation.
Eliminates the need for clinical judgement.
Prevents misunderstandings and improves patient safety.

questions.rationale: Clear communication reduces errors, improves teamwork, and contributes to safer, higher-quality patient care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best describes evidence-informed nursing practice?

options.text: Following only physician instructions.
Combining current evidence, clinical expertise and patient preferences.
Following outdated routines.
Relying only on personal experience.

questions.rationale: Evidence-informed nursing integrates research evidence, professional expertise, and patient values to provide the highest quality care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse is asked to perform a procedure that they have never been trained to undertake. What is the most appropriate response?

options.text: Decline the procedure and seek appropriate supervision or training.
Perform the procedure if the patient agrees.
Ask another nurse to sign the documentation.
Perform the procedure carefully.

questions.rationale: Nurses are professionally accountable for practising within their scope of competence. Seeking guidance or supervision protects patient safety and demonstrates professional responsibility.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which action best demonstrates patient advocacy?

options.text: Speaking up when a patient's safety is at risk.
Following every medical order without question.
Avoiding discussions with patients about treatment options.
Allowing family members to make all decisions.

questions.rationale: Patient advocacy involves protecting patients' rights, ensuring their voices are heard, and acting when patient safety or wellbeing is threatened.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient refuses a prescribed medication. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Discard the medication and leave.
Document the refusal without discussion.
Explore the patient's concerns and provide appropriate education.
Force the patient to take the medication.

questions.rationale: Patients have the right to refuse treatment. The nurse should first determine the reason for refusal, provide education, and support informed decision-making before documenting the outcome.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which characteristic is essential for maintaining professional boundaries?

options.text: Maintaining respectful and therapeutic relationships.
Accepting expensive gifts from patients.
Becoming close personal friends with patients.
Sharing personal financial information.

questions.rationale: Professional boundaries protect both the patient and the nurse by ensuring that relationships remain therapeutic, respectful, and focused on patient care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse notices a colleague documenting care that was not provided. What is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Ignore the situation.
Confront the colleague publicly.
Follow organisational policy by reporting the concern appropriately.
Change the documentation yourself.

questions.rationale: Falsification of documentation is a serious professional and legal issue. Nurses have a responsibility to report concerns through appropriate organisational procedures.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Professional appearance is important because it:

options.text: Is only required during inspections.
Builds patient confidence and promotes professionalism.
Helps nurses appear more authoritative.
Has no impact on patient care.

questions.rationale: Professional appearance contributes to patient trust, confidence, infection prevention, and the professional image of nursing.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which behaviour demonstrates effective teamwork?

options.text: Sharing important patient information during handover.
Withholding concerns until the next shift.
Completing all work independently.
Avoiding communication with other healthcare professionals.

questions.rationale: Effective teamwork depends on timely communication, collaboration, and sharing accurate patient information to ensure continuity of care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse accidentally administers the wrong dose of medication but the patient experiences no immediate harm. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Inform the patient only if symptoms develop.
Wait until the next shift to inform the manager.
Report the medication error immediately and monitor the patient.
Keep the incident confidential.

questions.rationale: Medication errors and near misses must be reported promptly to protect the patient, initiate appropriate treatment if necessary, and improve healthcare systems.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best describes lifelong learning in nursing?

options.text: Nurses continually update their knowledge and skills throughout their careers.
Education finishes after graduation.
Learning is only necessary when changing jobs.
Nurses only learn when required by employers.

questions.rationale: Healthcare continually evolves. Lifelong learning helps nurses maintain competence, deliver evidence-informed care, and meet professional standards.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A professional nurse demonstrates integrity by:

options.text: Completing documentation before providing care.
Sharing confidential information with colleagues during breaks.
Avoiding responsibility when mistakes occur.
Being honest, ethical, and accountable in all professional activities.

questions.rationale: Integrity is a core professional value. It involves honesty, accountability, ethical behaviour, and consistently acting in the best interests of patients.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Before administering any medication, what is the nurse's FIRST responsibility?

options.text: Check the expiry date
Verify the patient's identity using approved identifiers
Prepare the medication tray
Explain the medication

questions.rationale: Correct patient identification is the first step in preventing medication errors. Nurses should follow organisational policy by using at least two approved patient identifiers before administering medications.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse enters a patient's room and finds water spilled on the floor. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Tell housekeeping to clean it later.
Remove the hazard immediately or ensure it is cleaned.
Continue with patient care.
Place a chair over the spill.

questions.rationale: Removing environmental hazards immediately helps prevent patient falls and promotes a safe healthcare environment.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which patient is at the highest risk of experiencing a fall?

options.text: An elderly patient receiving sedative medication.
A middle-aged visitor.
A healthy young adult.
A nurse completing documentation.

questions.rationale: Older adults taking sedatives are at significantly higher risk of falls due to impaired balance, reduced alertness, and slower reaction times.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: When assisting a patient to stand, the nurse should:

options.text: Twist while lifting.
Lock the bed and wheelchair brakes before transfer.
Stand several steps away.
Pull the patient quickly by the arms.

questions.rationale: Locking equipment prevents unexpected movement and reduces the risk of falls during patient transfers.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient rings the call bell requesting assistance to the bathroom. The nurse is busy with documentation. What is the BEST action?

options.text: Tell the patient to walk independently.
Ask the patient to wait until documentation is complete.
Ignore the call bell.
Respond promptly or arrange assistance.

questions.rationale: Responding promptly to patient requests helps prevent falls, promotes dignity, and demonstrates patient-centred care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which action best demonstrates safe body mechanics?

options.text: Twist while lifting.
Keep your feet together.
Keep the load close to your body.
Bend from the waist.

questions.rationale: Keeping the load close to the body reduces spinal strain and improves balance during lifting or moving activities.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient has remained in bed for several days. Which nursing action best prevents pressure injuries?

options.text: Reposition the patient regularly.
Encourage long periods of uninterrupted sleep.
Limit fluid intake.
Massage reddened skin.

questions.rationale: Regular repositioning reduces prolonged pressure on tissues and is one of the most effective methods of preventing pressure injuries.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which patient requires the highest level of pressure injury prevention?

options.text: Visitor waiting in the reception area.
Patient attending an outpatient appointment.
Patient with limited mobility following a stroke.
Independent patient walking daily.

questions.rationale: Patients with limited mobility are unable to relieve pressure independently and are at greater risk of developing pressure injuries.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient suddenly reports severe chest pain while walking. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Complete documentation first.
Offer food.
Assist the patient to rest and assess immediately.
Encourage the patient to continue walking.

questions.rationale: Chest pain may indicate a life-threatening condition. The nurse should stop activity, assess the patient promptly, and initiate appropriate emergency procedures.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best reflects a culture of patient safety?

options.text: Mistakes should be hidden whenever possible.
Near misses should not be reported.
Incident reporting is only for serious injuries.
Staff should report safety concerns to improve patient care.

questions.rationale: Reporting incidents and near misses supports organisational learning and helps prevent future patient harm.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse is preparing to administer medication. Which of the following is one of the recognised medication rights?

options.text: Right hospital
Right patient
Right visitor
Right diagnosis

questions.rationale: The "Right Patient" is one of the fundamental medication administration rights that helps reduce medication errors.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which action should the nurse take when using a wheelchair?

options.text: Leave the footrests down during transfers.
Lock the wheelchair brakes before transfer.
Push the wheelchair as quickly as possible.
Allow the patient to stand without assistance.

questions.rationale: Locking wheelchair brakes ensures stability during patient transfers and reduces the risk of falls.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse notices that a patient's bed is in the highest position after care has been completed. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Leave it as it is.
Raise the side rails only.
Ask another nurse to check later.
Lower the bed and ensure safety measures are in place.

questions.rationale: Keeping the bed in its lowest safe position helps reduce injury should a patient attempt to get out of bed independently.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse discovers smoke coming from an electrical device. According to the RACE principle, what is the FIRST action?

options.text: Close all windows.
Call the patient's family.
Rescue anyone in immediate danger.
Extinguish the fire.

questions.rationale: RACE stands for Rescue, Alarm, Contain and Extinguish/Evacuate. Protecting people from immediate danger is always the priority.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which action best promotes safe medication administration?

options.text: Administering medication without reading the label.
Leaving medications at the bedside for later.
Preparing medications for several patients at the same time.
Checking the medication label carefully before administration.

questions.rationale: Carefully checking medication labels helps prevent medication errors and supports patient safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient appears dizzy while walking. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Assist the patient to sit safely and assess the condition.
Leave the patient alone.
Continue walking to the destination.
Encourage faster walking.

questions.rationale: Stopping activity and ensuring patient safety helps prevent falls while allowing the nurse to assess the cause of dizziness.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Why should nurses document patient care promptly?

options.text: To satisfy patients.
To reduce paperwork later.
Documentation is optional.
To ensure accurate communication and continuity of care.

questions.rationale: Accurate and timely documentation supports communication, legal accountability, and continuity of patient care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient with impaired mobility needs assistance transferring from bed to chair. Which equipment provides additional safety?

options.text: Blood pressure cuff.
Stethoscope.
Thermometer.
Gait belt.

questions.rationale: A gait belt improves control during transfers and helps reduce the risk of patient and staff injury.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which behaviour contributes most to a positive patient safety culture?

options.text: Ignoring minor incidents.
Blaming staff for mistakes.
Encouraging open communication about safety concerns.
Reporting only major accidents.

questions.rationale: Open communication encourages learning, supports continuous improvement, and strengthens patient safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse notices a colleague bypassing the patient identification process to save time. What is the BEST action?

options.text: Remind the colleague of the correct procedure and escalate if necessary.
Ignore the behaviour.
Tell other staff members.
Complete the identification on behalf of the colleague.

questions.rationale: All nurses share responsibility for maintaining patient safety. Addressing unsafe practices promptly helps prevent errors and reinforces a culture of safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: What is the single most effective method of preventing the spread of infection in healthcare settings?

options.text: Cleaning patient rooms daily
Wearing a surgical mask
Hand hygiene before and after patient contact
Wearing gloves at all times

questions.rationale: Hand hygiene is recognised worldwide as the most effective measure for preventing healthcare-associated infections. It should be performed before and after every patient contact and after contact with body fluids or contaminated surfaces.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse removes gloves after providing patient care. What should the nurse do NEXT?

options.text: Prepare medications.
Remove the uniform.
Touch the patient's bed rails.
Perform hand hygiene.

questions.rationale: Gloves do not replace hand hygiene. Hands should always be cleaned immediately after glove removal because microscopic contamination may still occur.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: When should a nurse perform hand hygiene?

options.text: Before and after patient contact and whenever hands may be contaminated.
Only before patient contact.
Only after patient contact.
At the beginning of the shift only.

questions.rationale: Hand hygiene should be performed at multiple points during patient care to reduce the transmission of microorganisms.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) should always be selected according to the anticipated exposure risk?

options.text: Randomly selected PPE
Appropriate PPE based on the expected exposure to blood, body fluids or infectious materials
Gloves only
Face shield only

questions.rationale: PPE selection depends on the type of patient care being provided and the likelihood of exposure to infectious material.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient has a suspected infectious respiratory illness. Which action best helps prevent transmission?

options.text: Encourage visitors without precautions.
Leave the patient in a crowded waiting room.
Apply appropriate transmission-based precautions.
Remove all PPE before entering the room.

questions.rationale: Transmission-based precautions provide additional protection beyond standard precautions when caring for patients with known or suspected infectious diseases.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which action contaminates a sterile field?

options.text: Keeping the sterile field within sight.
Reaching across the sterile field.
Keeping the sterile field above waist level.
Opening sterile packages carefully.

questions.rationale: Reaching over a sterile field may allow microorganisms from clothing or skin to contaminate sterile equipment.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse preparing a sterile dressing notices that the sterile package has a small tear. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Discard the package and obtain a new sterile item.
Use the package carefully.
Cover the tear with tape.
Ask another nurse if it is acceptable.

questions.rationale: Any damage to sterile packaging compromises sterility. The item should not be used.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement about sterile technique is CORRECT?

options.text: Sterile fields may be left unattended.
Sterile gloves eliminate the need for aseptic technique.
Sterile items may touch clean surfaces.
Moisture can contaminate a sterile field.

questions.rationale: Moisture allows microorganisms to travel through packaging by capillary action, contaminating the sterile field.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: When caring for a patient with an indwelling urinary catheter, which nursing action best reduces the risk of infection?

options.text: Raise the drainage bag above bladder level.
Disconnect the drainage tubing daily.
Maintain a closed drainage system.
Irrigate the catheter routinely.

questions.rationale: Maintaining a closed urinary drainage system significantly reduces the risk of catheter-associated urinary tract infections (CAUTIs).

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: The urinary drainage bag should always be positioned:

options.text: Below the level of the bladder.
At the same height as the bladder.
On the patient's bed.
Above the bladder.

questions.rationale: Keeping the drainage bag below bladder level prevents urine backflow and reduces infection risk.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which action demonstrates correct respiratory hygiene?

options.text: Covering the mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing and performing hand hygiene afterwards.
Sneezing into your hands.
Coughing openly.
Removing your mask to cough.

questions.rationale: Respiratory hygiene reduces the spread of respiratory infections and protects patients and healthcare workers.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Why should reusable patient equipment be cleaned between patients?

options.text: To reduce healthcare-associated infections.
To make storage easier.
To improve appearance.
To reduce paperwork.

questions.rationale: Cleaning and disinfecting reusable equipment prevents cross-contamination between patients.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which patient requires the nurse to be especially vigilant regarding infection prevention?

options.text: Healthy visitor.
Patient with a weakened immune system.
Young athlete.
Hospital volunteer.

questions.rationale: Immunocompromised patients are more susceptible to infections and require strict adherence to infection prevention practices.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse accidentally touches the outside of a sterile glove with bare fingers while putting it on. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Continue the procedure.
Remove the glove and begin again with a new sterile glove.
Ask another nurse to complete the procedure.
Wipe the glove with alcohol.

questions.rationale: Touching the outside of a sterile glove with bare hands contaminates the glove, requiring replacement.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: What is the purpose of Standard Precautions?

options.text: To replace hand hygiene.
To reduce the risk of transmission of microorganisms from all patients.
To apply only to patients with confirmed infections.
To eliminate the need for PPE.

questions.rationale: Standard Precautions are applied to every patient because any individual may carry infectious microorganisms.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Before preparing a sterile procedure, the nurse should FIRST:

options.text: Apply sterile gloves.
Complete documentation.
Wash or sanitise hands thoroughly.
Arrange the patient's pillows.

questions.rationale: Hand hygiene is the first step in preventing contamination before any aseptic procedure.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which action is appropriate when disposing of a used needle?

options.text: Bend the needle before disposal.
Recap the needle carefully.
Wrap it in paper before disposal.
Place it immediately into an approved sharps container.

questions.rationale: Sharps should be disposed of immediately into approved puncture-resistant containers to reduce needlestick injuries.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse notices that hand sanitiser is not effective because the hands are visibly soiled. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water.
Wear gloves.
Dry hands with paper towels only.
Apply extra sanitiser.

questions.rationale: Soap and water should be used whenever hands are visibly dirty or contaminated.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which nursing action best prevents cross-contamination between patients?

options.text: Changing gloves and performing hand hygiene between patient contacts.
Wearing an apron only.
Wearing the same gloves between patients.
Using the same equipment without cleaning.

questions.rationale: Changing gloves and cleaning hands between patients interrupts the chain of infection.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best describes infection prevention in nursing practice?

options.text: Only doctors are responsible for preventing infections.
Infection prevention is the responsibility of every healthcare worker during every patient interaction.
Infection prevention is mainly the responsibility of infection control nurses.
Infection prevention is only important during outbreaks.

questions.rationale: Every healthcare professional shares responsibility for preventing infections by consistently following evidence-based infection prevention and control practices.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse is introducing themselves to a newly admitted patient. Which approach demonstrates therapeutic communication?

options.text: "Hello, my name is Sarah. I'll be your nurse today. How would you like me to address you?"
"You don't need to worry about asking questions."
"Please don't interrupt while I'm working."
"I'm very busy today, so let's make this quick."

questions.rationale: Introducing oneself respectfully and asking the patient's preferred form of address establishes trust, rapport, and a therapeutic nurse-patient relationship.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient appears anxious before surgery. What is the nurse's BEST response?

options.text: "You should try to relax."
"Many people feel anxious before surgery. Would you like to tell me what concerns you most?"
"You'll be asleep anyway."
"There's nothing to worry about."

questions.rationale: Acknowledging emotions and encouraging patients to express concerns demonstrates empathy and therapeutic communication.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Active listening involves:

options.text: Looking at documentation while the patient speaks.
Finishing the patient's sentences.
Giving full attention, maintaining eye contact, and responding appropriately.
Interrupting to offer advice.

questions.rationale: Active listening helps nurses understand patients' concerns, improves trust, and enhances the quality of care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: When communicating with a patient who has hearing impairment, the nurse should:

options.text: Speak loudly into the patient's ear.
Communicate only through family members.
Face the patient while speaking clearly at a normal pace.
Avoid eye contact.

questions.rationale: Facing the patient allows them to observe facial expressions and lip movements, improving communication without unnecessary shouting.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A nurse is preparing to assist a patient with personal hygiene. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Leave the room to collect equipment later.
Close the curtains and maintain the patient's privacy.
Remove the patient's clothing immediately.
Begin washing without explanation.

questions.rationale: Maintaining privacy preserves dignity and demonstrates respect before commencing personal care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which nursing action best promotes patient dignity during bathing?

options.text: Allow visitors to remain in the room.
Complete the bath as quickly as possible without speaking.
Expose the entire body for convenience.
Cover body areas not being washed.

questions.rationale: Maintaining body coverage during personal care protects dignity, privacy, and comfort.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient requires assistance with oral hygiene. Why is regular oral care important?

options.text: It replaces tooth brushing at home.
It is only necessary before discharge.
It only improves appearance.
It reduces the risk of infection and promotes comfort.

questions.rationale: Good oral hygiene promotes comfort, prevents infection, supports nutrition, and improves overall health.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient has difficulty swallowing fluids. What is the nurse's PRIORITY action?

options.text: Report the difficulty and follow swallowing safety precautions.
Encourage the patient to drink quickly.
Give fluids through a straw immediately.
Ignore the complaint.

questions.rationale: Difficulty swallowing (dysphagia) increases the risk of aspiration. Appropriate assessment and safety measures are essential.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which position is generally recommended when assisting a patient to eat?

options.text: Flat on the back.
Trendelenburg position.
Upright sitting position.
Semi-recumbent.

questions.rationale: An upright position promotes safe swallowing and reduces the risk of aspiration.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: During mealtime, the nurse notices a patient coughing repeatedly while eating. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Give water immediately.
Encourage the patient to continue eating.
Leave the patient alone.
Stop the meal and assess for swallowing difficulty.

questions.rationale: Persistent coughing during meals may indicate aspiration risk and requires immediate assessment.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient is unable to reposition independently in bed. What is the nurse's BEST action?

options.text: Assist with regular repositioning using safe techniques.
Raise the bed to the highest position.
Ask the patient to manage independently.
Leave the patient in one position.

questions.rationale: Regular repositioning improves comfort, circulation, and reduces the risk of pressure injuries.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: When assisting a patient to walk, the nurse should:

options.text: Encourage the patient to walk alone.
Hold only the patient's clothing.
Stay close to the patient's weaker side if assistance is needed.
Walk several metres ahead.

questions.rationale: Supporting the patient's weaker side improves stability and reduces fall risk during ambulation.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient asks a question that the nurse cannot answer confidently. What is the BEST response?

options.text: Change the subject.
Tell the patient you will find accurate information and return.
Ignore the question.
Guess the answer.

questions.rationale: Honesty and professional accountability require nurses to seek accurate information rather than guessing.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best demonstrates empathy?

options.text: "It's not a serious problem."
"I understand this is a difficult time for you."
"Everyone feels this way."
"You shouldn't worry."

questions.rationale: Empathy acknowledges the patient's feelings and helps build a trusting therapeutic relationship.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient refuses assistance with bathing. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.text: Leave without documentation.
Force the patient to bathe.
Explore the patient's reasons and respect their wishes while promoting hygiene.
Report the refusal immediately.

questions.rationale: Patients have the right to participate in decisions regarding their care. Understanding the reason for refusal allows appropriate support and education.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Why is accurate documentation after providing patient care important?

options.text: It communicates care provided and supports continuity of care.
It is only used for legal purposes.
It is optional.
It replaces verbal handover.

questions.rationale: Documentation provides an accurate record of care, facilitates communication among healthcare professionals, and supports patient safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: During handover, the nurse should communicate patient information that is:

options.text: Accurate, relevant, timely, and confidential.
Shared with everyone present.
Based on assumptions.
Limited to medication information only.

questions.rationale: Effective clinical handover relies on accurate and relevant information to ensure continuity and safety of patient care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient who speaks limited English is unable to understand important healthcare information. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Use a qualified interpreter according to organisational policy.
Avoid discussing the treatment.
Ask family members to interpret complex medical information.
Ask another patient to translate.

questions.rationale: Qualified interpreters help ensure accurate communication, informed consent, and patient safety.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: A patient begins crying while discussing their diagnosis. What is the nurse's MOST appropriate response?

options.text: Change the subject.
Tell the patient not to cry.
Leave the room immediately.
Sit quietly, acknowledge the patient's feelings, and offer support.

questions.rationale: Providing emotional support and allowing patients to express their feelings demonstrates compassionate, person-centred nursing care.

questions.programArea: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
questions.stem: Which statement best summarises effective nursing communication?

options.text: It depends mainly on completing documentation.
It combines listening, empathy, respect, clear information, and patient involvement.
It focuses mainly on giving instructions.
It is only necessary during admission.

questions.rationale: Effective nursing communication is a two-way process that includes active listening, empathy, respect, clear explanations, and involving patients in their care, leading to improved safety, satisfaction, and health outcomes.
